item.title: How We Split Our Tiny 34m² Bristol Living Room into a Proper Office and Relax Zone for Under £400
item.description:
If you live in a rented UK flat, you already know the drill. You sign the lease on a dreary Tuesday, move in three suitcases and five blue IKEA bags, and suddenly realize your entire living space is roughly the size of a disabled parking bay.

That was precisely our situation six months ago when my partner and I moved into a 34m² top-floor flat in Bristol. The building is a converted Victorian terrace, which sounds charming on Rightmove until you try hauling a mattress up three flights of spiral stairs that smell faintly of damp and old carpets.

item.title: 8 Folding Furniture Hacks That Actually Freed Up Space in My Tiny Flat
item.description:
8 Folding Furniture Hacks That Actually Freed Up Space in My Tiny Flat

I’ve lived in three flats under 35m² in the last six years — Leeds, then two in London — and if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that most “space-saving furniture” round-ups are written by people who’ve never actually had to eat dinner on their knees because there was nowhere to put a table.

So this isn’t a list pulled together from a manufacturer’s press pack. Everything below has lived in my flat, been folded and unfolded a hundred times, and in one case got returned within a fortnight because it was rubbish. I’ve tried to be honest about that too.

item.title: How I Finally Stopped Working from My Sofa (And Other Tiny Living Miracles)
item.description:
I’ll be honest with you: living in a small flat is basically a never-ending game of Tetris, except the blocks are your belongings and the stakes involve losing your sanity.

For the longest time, my main living space—a measly 15-square-metre box—was doing absolutely everything. I was eating lukewarm pasta on a laptop stand while sitting on the same sofa I used to watch Netflix on, all while surrounded by a pile of work paperwork that mocked me from the coffee table. It was, quite frankly, a bit of a nightmare.
